## Natural history notes

A tiny ground cricket characterized by a dark brown to black body, long antennae, short legs for quick hopping, and a soft chirping song produced close to the ground. In Florida, the Carolina Ground Cricket is found in leaf litter, grassy edges, gardens, fields, pine flatwoods, forest margins, marsh edges, and other low, humid habitats with cover. It feeds on small bits of plant material, fungi, seeds, and decaying organic matter, while serving as prey for spiders, frogs, lizards, birds, and predatory insects.
